excerpt: Commercial restroom work is priced three different ways: per restroom per visit for routine sanitizing, per fixture for descaling, and per hour or per sq ft for floor and grout restoration. This guide shows the national US ranges for each unit, the minimum charges that apply to small jobs, and a worked example you can copy into your own budget.
quickAnswer: Routine commercial restroom sanitization runs $15–$30 per restroom per visit nationally, while periodic descaling of toilets, urinals, and sinks typically prices at $16–$28 per fixture or $55–$95 per specialty labor hour. Tile floor and grout deep scrubbing adds $0.35–$0.75 per sq ft of restroom floor, and most vendors enforce a project minimum of roughly $110–$190 (two specialty hours) on top of the $90–$135 per-visit minimum for routine service.

blocks.text: The Three Unit Prices Vendors Use for Restroom Work

When a facility manager asks what restroom sanitization costs, the honest answer depends on which unit the vendor is pricing. Routine nightly or weekday restroom service is almost always priced per restroom per visit and rolled into the janitorial base contract. Descaling, which removes calcium, uric scale, and mineral rings from toilets, urinals, sinks, and flush valves, is priced per fixture or by specialty labor hour because the work time depends on how much scale has built up. Floor and grout restoration is priced per sq ft of restroom floor, since a 120 sq ft single-user restroom and a 650 sq ft multi-stall core restroom take very different amounts of machine time.

Mixing these units is the most common reason two quotes for the same building look wildly different. One vendor may show $22 per restroom per visit and a separate $480 quarterly descaling line; another may show $34 per restroom per visit with descaling quietly blended in. Normalize every bid to the same unit before you compare.

blocks.text: How Per-Fixture Descaling Rates Are Built

Vendors arrive at per-fixture pricing by working backward from specialty labor. A trained technician using an acid-based bowl and urinal descaler, pumice stones for rings, and a scale-rated brush set will typically complete three to four fixtures per hour, including dwell time, agitation, rinse, and a final disinfectant pass with an EPA-registered product. At $55–$95 per hour, that math produces the $16–$28 per fixture band. Heavily scaled urinals with clogged traps or blocked waterless cartridges push the job toward the top of the range or onto hourly billing.

Sinks and countertops are usually counted as fixtures, but some vendors split them into a cheaper sub-rate of $10–$16 because faucet aerators and drains descale faster than a urinal throat. Ask for the fixture inventory in writing so you are not billed for 30 fixtures in a building with 22.

blocks.title: Benchmark: labor time per restroom
blocks.text: Routine restroom service averages 0.15–0.25 labor hours per restroom per visit, which is why the $15–$30 per-visit band holds across most US markets. If a bid implies less than 9 minutes per multi-stall restroom, expect skipped tasks such as partition wiping, dispenser restocking, or floor drain flushing.
Worked Example: 18,000 Sq Ft Office With Four Restrooms

Consider an 18,000 sq ft suburban office with four multi-stall restrooms holding 10 toilets, 4 urinals, and 8 sinks (22 fixtures), plus 720 sq ft of ceramic tile restroom flooring. The tenant wants weekday cleaning and quarterly descaling with grout scrubbing. Using 4.33 weeks per month, five visits per week equals 21.65 visits per month.

blocks.caption: Monthly and annual budget for an 18,000 sq ft office with 22 restroom fixtures

blocks.text: Notice that routine service dwarfs the periodic descaling cost. That is normal, and it is also why buyers should not let a vendor cut corners on descaling to win a bid: skipping it for a year usually doubles the next descaling event because uric scale hardens and traps odor-causing bacteria inside urinal throats.
Tools That Signal a Vendor Is Equipped for the Work

Restroom descaling itself is mostly chemistry and hand tools, but restroom soil does not stay in the restroom. Corridor carpet outside restroom doors absorbs tracked moisture and urine residue, and a vendor who prices restroom programs well usually carries heated spot extraction for those transition zones. Equipment worth asking about includes the Bissell BigGreen Commercial BG10, a 10.5-in path upright with dual 1.75-gal tanks and two motors for flushing corridor lanes; the Hoover Commercial Spotter CH84000, a 13 lb portable with a stainless upholstery tool for lounge seating near restroom vestibules; and the Mytee S-300H Tempo, a 1-gallon spotter with a 210F heater and 55 PSI pump that breaks down organic stains without over-wetting carpet backing.

items: Ask whether the vendor's descaler is compatible with your fixture finishes; chrome flush valves and brushed nickel faucets can etch under strong hydrochloric products.
Confirm the disinfectant used after descaling is EPA-registered with a stated dwell time, typically 3–10 minutes for restroom surfaces.
Request color-coded microfiber (red for toilets and urinals) to prevent cross-contamination into breakrooms.
Verify that floor drains are flushed with enzyme treatment during each grout event to control sewer-gas odor.

blocks.text: Compliance and Contract Language That Affects Price

Acid descalers fall under the OSHA Hazard Communication Standard, so the vendor must keep current Safety Data Sheets on site, label secondary spray bottles, and train staff on splash PPE. Restroom technicians also fall within OSHA bloodborne pathogen exposure planning when they handle sharps containers, feminine hygiene units, or bodily fluid cleanup. Vendors who carry these programs properly spend more on training and PPE, which is one reason the bottom of the $15–$30 range rarely includes them.

blocks.title: Insurance and scope checks
blocks.text: Require a certificate of insurance listing your company or landlord as additional insured with at least $1 million per occurrence general liability, plus workers' compensation. Spell out in the scope whether descaling chemistry, grout sealer, and feminine hygiene unit servicing are included or billed separately.
How to Use These Unit Prices When You Request Bids

items.name: Inventory fixtures and floor area
items.text: Count toilets, urinals, sinks, and showers per restroom, and measure tile floor area. Give every bidder the same sheet.

items.name: Separate routine from periodic
items.text: Ask for routine restroom pricing per restroom per visit and periodic descaling per fixture, with grout scrub per sq ft.

items.name: State the frequency
items.text: Specify visits per week and descaling cadence so bidders calculate monthly totals using the same 4.33 weeks-per-month factor.

items.name: Normalize to annual cost
items.text: Convert every bid to a 12-month figure including amortized periodic work before comparing.

faqs.q: Is restroom descaling the same as routine restroom sanitization?
faqs.a: No. Routine sanitization covers daily or weekday tasks such as disinfecting toilet seats, flush handles, partitions, and sinks, restocking paper and soap, and damp mopping. Descaling is a periodic project that removes mineral and uric scale from bowls, urinal throats, and faucets with acid chemistry. Routine service is priced at $15–$30 per restroom per visit; descaling is priced at $16–$28 per fixture per event.

faqs.q: Why do some vendors charge a minimum for a small descaling job?
faqs.a: Mobilization, PPE, and chemical handling cost the same whether the technician descales four fixtures or twenty. Most vendors set a project minimum equal to about two specialty labor hours, or $110–$190, so a two-restroom suite with four fixtures pays the minimum rather than the per-fixture rate.

faqs.q: What OSHA requirements apply to restroom sanitization crews?
faqs.a: The Hazard Communication Standard requires Safety Data Sheets, labeled containers, and training for acid descalers and disinfectants. The Bloodborne Pathogens Standard applies when crews may contact blood or other potentially infectious materials, which means exposure control plans, gloves, and Hepatitis B vaccination offers. Ask vendors to confirm both programs in writing.

faqs.q: How do I convert a per-visit restroom price to a monthly budget?
faqs.a: Multiply restrooms by the per-visit price, then by visits per month. Visits per month equal visits per week times 4.33. Three restrooms at $20 per visit, five times weekly, equals 3 × $20 × 21.65, or about $1,299 per month.

faqs.q: Do green-certified restroom products cost more?
faqs.a: Green Seal or EPA Safer Choice certified cleaners usually add little to the per-visit rate because concentrated dilution keeps chemical cost under a few cents per restroom. Certified descalers can require longer dwell times, which may add 5–10 percent to periodic descaling labor.
